newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: Mongolia sees deal on Kazakhstan copper dispute.
newsitem.headline: Mongolia sees deal on Kazakhstan copper dispute.

text.p: Mongolia's main copper exporter Erdenet Concern said on Wednesday it expected to reach an accord with Kazakhstan's Balkhash Copper Plant in a dispute over unsettled payments for a shipment of Mongolian copper.
Erdenet Concern sales manager Zorig said the Balkhash Copper plant had failed to pay for or return 9,600 tonnes of copper concentrate it imported from Mongolia in April.
"We have discussed this issue, and the debt will be paid," Zorig told Reuters in an interview.
The copper shipment was worth $26.96 million at world market prices at the time of export, Zorig said.
Balkhash officials could not be reached for comment.
Erdenet and Balkhash were negotiating whether the payment would be made in refined copper or U.S. dollars, said Purvee, chief of Erdenet's trade department.
"We are discussing the price and the form of payment at the moment with Balkhash," Purvee said.
If Balkhash made the payment in refined copper, Erdenet would deduct processing costs, he said.
Erdenet is a Mongolian-Russian joint venture and most of its exports go to Russian refineries.
"Annually we sell 450,000 to 460,000 tonnes of copper concentrate to them at world market prices," Zorig said.
"In addition to this we sell small amounts on an irregular basis to other countries," he said.
Mongolia's exports of copper concentrate were 411,800 tonnes in January to October, up from 359,000 tonnes in the year-ago period, official statistics show.
